title: Brandon McNulty Pulls Off a Miracle to Win Cycling's World Title
summary:
Have you ever done something so hard that you didn't believe it was real until the very end? That's exactly what happened to Brandon McNulty on Sunday in Montreal.

The 28-year-old American cyclist won the elite road race at the UCI Road World Championships. He became the first American man to win this title since Lance Armstrong in 1993.

McNulty made his big move with 33 kilometres left. Then he just kept pedalling. And pedalling. For more than six hours total, his legs spun around and around.

"Until the last 300 metres, I really didn't even believe it," McNulty said. "I was just dying, but I just kept pushing."

At one point, his lead shrank to only 10 seconds. The other riders were chasing him hard. But nobody could catch him. He finished in 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds. Michael Matthews of Australia got silver, 13 seconds behind.

McNulty called it a miracle. "We've said for weeks that we have a super strong team," he said. "I guess today, a miracle happened."

Even Armstrong congratulated him. Not bad for a guy who wasn't even one of the favourites!
why_it_matters: It shows that even when you are not the person everyone expects to win, refusing to stop — pedal after pedal for six hours — can lead to something amazing.

background_read: The UCI Road World Championships (a yearly race where the best cyclists from many countries ride to become world champion) is one of the biggest prizes in cycling.
The winner of the road race gets to wear a special rainbow-striped jersey for a whole year, so everyone can see they are the world champion.
Montreal (a large city in Canada) hosted this year's race, and Lance Armstrong (a famous American cyclist from the 1990s and 2000s) was the last American man to win the title before McNulty.
Article_Structure: WHO: Brandon McNulty, a 28-year-old American cyclist, racing against the world's best riders, including Michael Matthews of Australia.
WHAT: He won the elite road race at the UCI Road World Championships, making his big move with 33 kilometres left and finishing in 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds.
WHERE: The race was held in Montreal, Canada.
WHY: He became the first American man to win the title since 1993, even though he was not one of the favourites — he called it a miracle.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled because the USA had waited since 1993 for another men's world champion, and McNulty was not even one of the favourites.
They worked hard and cut his lead to just 10 seconds, but they could not catch him, so they may feel they let the title slip away.
A rider staying away alone for 33 kilometres is very rare in modern racing, because the big group usually catches one lonely rider.
